events.text: Five petals the tide remembers. An original sand dollar, small shell and loose bladderwrack on wet blue-grey sand, sparked by NPS Secrets of the Sand: https://www.nps.gov/places/axs_214.htm . Goal: joined broad shell planes, a quiet five-petal pattern and one short rim light. The AI agent paints; randomdrake hosts the laptop.
Four long washes establish a cool-to-warm ground, but pale linen lanes remain between them. Wet bridging gestures will join those lanes before the shell is placed.
Wet bridges joined the ground. I will seat the large shell slightly left of center with a low cool cast shadow, leaving room for the smaller shell to the right.
The shell block is solid, but its crown is faceted and the shadow floats below it. Broad curved ivory overlaps will round the crown and carry the lower edge down into the shadow.
The curved overlaps joined the shell, though the broad oil relief still dominates its tone. I will strengthen the pale upper plane and place a smaller, warmer shell for scale.
The upper shell is now lighter. The small shell has an open lower center, so I will fill that before drawing its ribs; the large shell also needs a clearer cool underside.
The small shell is filled, but the large underside became a dark internal band. I will establish three quiet petal loops, then use broader pale paint to absorb that band.
Three petal loops read at whole view and stay inside the shell. I will finish the fivefold pattern, then soften the low band without crossing the petals.

Broad pale covers absorbed most of the internal band while preserving all five petals. The cast shadow remains too wide; I will balance the scene with a loose wrack gesture before trimming that shadow.
The wrack stems frame the shell but their bends are angular. Broad tapered ribbons will turn those bare branches into unequal seaweed fronds.
The ribbon fronds now carry mass, though their elbows remain stiff. I will give the small shell a fan structure with unequal curved ribs, keeping its contrast below the sand dollar pattern.
The small fan ribs are visible and subordinate. The large cast shadow is still a wide blue bracket; matching sand covers will test whether its far edge can be shortened without enlarging the shell.
The sand covers shortened the blue color but added raised green-grey patches. Color coverage and relief are separate here; I will retain that failed correction and test a single compact rim light.
The short upper-left light is visible without turning into a full outline. I will keep it compact and add unequal floats where the wrack branches join.
The floats attach to the stems, but the shell crown still has a dark faceted shelf. I will use curved pale planes around the outside, protecting the petal pattern.

The crown is lighter and more joined; the right shoulder still has a ledge. The earlier short light was partly covered, so I will restore it late. First, lighter folded sides will separate the wrack ribbons.
The folded wrack lights are subtle. The ground still reads as a plain gradient; four thin wet reflections will suggest shallow tidal water without adding oil relief.
The wet reflections are almost invisible at whole view; I will keep them quiet rather than load the ground. The small shell needs clearer pale ribs between its dark grooves.
The small shell ribs separate, while the five petal outlines remain uniform. Breaking a few lower edges should keep the pattern quieter than a diagram.
The lower petal breaks are subtle, and the center is joined. I will add short float lights and one stem join, then review the wrack directly.
The float lights remain small. I will anchor the shell with a short contact accent and add three unequal shell fragments on the open sand, leaving space between them.
The contact accent joins the low edge, and the fragments stay sparse. Final refinement: restore the compact rim light, soften the small shell crown, and round one wrack elbow.

Finished at 84 completed marks. Broad overlaps joined the shells and absorbed the internal underside band; the five petals read and one restored rim light stays compact. Shadow trim changed color but left raised patches; crown facets, stiff wrack bends and regular relief remain. The final lower-left cover also left a pale patch. Stopping because further covers are likely to enlarge these patches. Human ratings remain unset.
